trust_decision.summary: On an uninitialized instance (no administrator user), anyone reaching the public /restore or /users/admin/init route is trusted to restore the DB or create the first admin; the only check is 'no admin exists yet', in each handler.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the unauthenticated restore endpoint; its handler only checks WasInitialized and then calls RestoreArchive.

fix_sites.entry_point: server start, passes token to backup/users/settings handlers
binary startup: token generated only if no --admin-password and no admin in DB (fix.diff:30-72)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: api/http/handler/users/admin_init.go:44 (route api/http/handler/users/handler.go:79): a second, independent way to become the first admin on an uninitialized instance, in a different package from the reported restore route

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The public /users/admin/init is the documented first-run setup wizard, it is not the reported restore route, so gating it can be argued to break intended onboarding.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: First-run wizard must still be able to create the admin and restore a backup with no user existing (with the correct token); --admin-password startup path and --no-setup-token must bypass the gate; restore on an initialized instance must still return 400; /api/settings/public must stay public. Changing /restore to RestrictedAccess or AdminAccess breaks first-run restore entirely.

O6_input_shapes: X-Setup-Token header with wrong value -> 403, constant-time compare (fix.diff:220-226, 450)
expected token empty (admin already exists at startup, --admin-password given, or --no-setup-token) -> gate disabled (fix.diff:445-447, 64, 35-37)
JSON body (admin init) vs multipart form (restore) on the two routes

O7_producer.where: fix.diff:30-54 and fix.diff:63-72 (token resolved at startup from --setup-token/env or generated, in api/cmd/portainer/main.go); flags at fix.diff:9-10

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second public restore route on the uninitialized instance (e.g. restore from S3 / remote URL) that calls operations.RestoreArchive with only the WasInitialized check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Portainer's business edition ships an S3 restore next to the file restore; a maintainer porting it would copy the existing public restore handler, including its access policy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A deprecated alias route (like the existing deprecated public /status alias) that forwards to adminInit or restore.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The codebase already keeps deprecated public aliases for backward compatibility; an alias for an older admin-init path is in the same style, and a solver could dismiss it as legacy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A lower-level restore path (e.g. restore-on-startup from a file flag or a public helper that wraps RestoreArchive) reachable without the handler gate.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: main.go already has DB-restore-related startup code (api/cmd/portainer/main.go:153); a maintainer could add a restore entry that bypasses the HTTP handler.
